newsitem.title: USA: American Real Estate undervalued -- money managers.
newsitem.headline: American Real Estate undervalued -- money managers.

text.p: Money managers such as John Spears of Tweedy Browne believe that American Real Estate Partners LP provides an attractive way to invest with Wall Street wheeler-dealer Carl Icahn, who controls it, Barron's said.

"The stock seems dirt cheap to us," Spears, a Tweedy Browne partner, told the investor weekly newspaper, as quoted in its June 2 edition. "Most REITs sell for more than the value of their properties. This company trades for less."
Icahn holds about 54 percent of American Real Estate, and has begun to use it to make investments other than real estate, Barron's said.

"American Real Estate Partners amounts to an undervalued real-estate portfolio married to a hedge fund run by Carl Icahn," Hugh Lamle of M.D. Sass Investor Services told Barron's. "You couldn't hire Icahn to manage your money. But here's a way to get his expertise at a cheap price."
American Real Estate shares closed up 1/4 to 11-3/8 on Friday. Spears told Barron's that the company is worth about $20 per share, while Lamle values it at $17.
